messages.subject: lambda0 shrinking
parts:
Hi folks,

Just wondering, is it a good thing or a bad thing if your estimate of lambda0, detection function intercept, is slowing shrinking?

 

I’m using the moving.fit function in openCR in an attempt to estimate density of golden bandicoots in a fenced reserve. Sigma is staying reasonable as are the density estimates. Lambda0 and sigma are held constant within the window in this model.

I use supposedly single-catch cage traps for catching bandicoots, but marsupials are very friendly and we sometimes get 2 animals in one trap, so I use multi-catch traps in the model.

 

moving_JSSAsecrD<-moving.fit(capthist=IA,mask=mask.clipped,type='JSSAsecrD',ncores=4,model=list(phi~t,D~t,lambda0~t,sigma~t), width = 5, centres = NULL, filestem = "Global_BLinterference_andothers_removed_JSSAsecrD_width5_2012_2019_IA",trace = FALSE, FUN = openCR.fit)

messages.subject: Re: lambda0 shrinking
parts:
My reaction is Why worry? Noting (i) the difference is only between ~0.01 and ~0.025 (ii) a bit hard to read as the rows of your table are not in chronological order (iii) what matters is probably lambda0 x sigma^2, so differences in sigma may matter more than you think and partly balance diferences in lambda0.
Murray
